---
title: "stateMINT: the emulator"
---

`estimint` ends at a single number, the EIR at the point a campaign is deployed.
`stateMINT` starts there. Given that EIR, the setting it belongs to, and the campaign
under evaluation, it returns the prevalence and clinical-case trajectories over six
years, three before the campaign and three after.

Those trajectories belong to an individual-based malaria transmission model, the lineage
implemented in [`malariasimulation`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/malariasimulation/). That
simulation is slow. A single scenario takes minutes of computation. A grid of net products
crossed with coverages crossed with resistance levels is a cluster job. `stateMINT` is trained
on a large library of those runs and reproduces their output in milliseconds. A fifty-scenario
batch takes under a second on a laptop CPU. Like any emulator, it is trustworthy only inside
the range of settings it was trained on.

The trained weights are not shipped in the wheel. They live on Hugging Face at
[`dide-ic/stateMINT`](https://huggingface.co/dide-ic/stateMINT), as two separate checkpoints,
one for prevalence and one for cases, of about 38 MB each. The first call downloads them and
caches them. Every later call reads the cache.

## Inputs and outputs

The input is twelve numbers rather than a time series, twelve scalars describing the setting
and the campaign. From them the emulator reconstructs the time grid itself, switches the
campaign on at the right day, and rolls the state forward.

The output is an array of shape `(B, 157)`, one row per scenario, 157 fortnightly windows
per row, spanning day 2190 to day 4374 of the simulation. The campaign lands at day 3285.
That puts the three pre-campaign years at the front of every row and the three response
years at the back.

Prevalence and cases are two separately trained checkpoints. Asking for both means loading
both and calling each once, and no single call returns the pair. The pipeline in
[Running Scenarios](../06-scenarios/index.qmd) does both for you.

## The state-space name

The *state* in `stateMINT` is the state-space architecture (a Mamba2 layer carrying a
hidden state along the sequence) and not an epidemiological compartment. There is no S,
I or R here. The distinction is drawn out in [The models](../03-concepts/models.qmd).
